purpose: Compare the optimized bounded linearizability checker with an independent brute-force sequential reference over a frozen small-history corpus.

independence.reference_algorithm: Enumerate every permutation; reject permutations violating real-time precedence; apply separately implemented transitions with nondeterministic unknown outcomes.
independence.optimized_algorithm: Depth-first eligible-operation search with cached remaining-set/state pairs.
independence.warning: Agreement on a finite corpus is evidence, not proof.

comparison.failure: Decision disagreement, witness rejected by reference, invalid history, or UNKNOWN_LIMIT.
comparison.witness: Independently replay every positive witness through the reference contract.

explicit_non_claims: Does not qualify a real sink or prove production linearizability.
Does not prove either checker or the shared contract correct.
The three- and four-operation tiers are deterministic samples, not exhaustive.
Raw timestamps are meaningful only under the single-observer monotonic clock contract.
No performance comparison with Porcupine is conducted.
